metadata.case_name: CHEUNG MAU FA v. REGENT CONSTRUCTION CO LTD

plaintiff.education_level: little education in China without completing primary one

injuries.description: soft tissue sprain of the right ankle
source: It was not in dispute that Ms Cheung sustained soft tissue injury to her right ankle by virtue of the accident.
Dr Lau and Dr Lee both found that Ms Cheung sustained soft tissue sprain of the right ankle which was consistent with the mechanism of injury as described by her.

Starting from 31 May 2013, Ms Cheung was followed up at the East Kowloon Psychiatric Centre. During the first visit, Ms Cheung described that she had become fearful with vivid flashback of the accident. She said that she was afraid of cars when crossing roads and had palpation with shortness of breath. Ms Cheung was diagnosed to have sustained PTSD.

injuries.description: adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood
source: Both Dr Hung and Dr Law agreed that Ms Cheung suffered from adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood.

manifestations.description: Decreased range of motion in the right ankle
Pain on plantarflexion and dorsiflexion of the right ankle
Numbness in the right leg and right ankle
Unable to stand for more than 2 hours
Unable to walk for more than 35 to 40 minutes
Pain radiating up to the right knee
Interrupted sleep and nightmares of falling from height
Fearfulness and vivid flashback of the accident; afraid of cars and avoidance behaviour
Depressed mood, anxiety and social withdrawal

treatments_received.treatment: Accident & Emergency assessment and discharge same day
source: After the accident, Ms Cheung was taken to the Accident and Emergency Department of Tseung Kwan O Hospital where she was found to have sustained a sprain in the right ankle with decreased range of motion.
She was discharged on the same day with 6 days of sick leave.

treatments_received.treatment: X-ray imaging of the right ankle/foot and right leg
source: X-ray did not reveal any fracture or dislocation of the foot.
A further x-ray was taken of the right ankle on 13 July 2012 which showed a vague lucent line at the navicular bone but no fracture.
another x-ray was taken of the right leg on 4 January 2013 which confirmed the absence of any fracture.
Ms Cheung also started physiotherapy and occupational therapy at the same hospital, and was referred to the Kwong Wah Hospital for further follow up treatments.

work assessment conducted at the Occupational Therapy Department of the Kwong Wah Hospital on 28 November 2012 ... 'Ms Cheung's walking balance and tolerance, squatting ability and lifting capacity are far below her mentioned job demand'.

treatments_received.treatment: Psychiatric assessment and treatment (East Kowloon Psychiatric Centre)
source: Starting from 31 May 2013, Ms Cheung was followed up at the East Kowloon Psychiatric Centre.
Both Dr Hung and Dr Law agreed that Ms Cheung suffered from adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood.

treatments_received.treatment: Pain clinic assessment and pain management
source: On 14 August 2014, Ms Cheung attended the pain clinic of Queen Elizabeth Hospital for pain management.
Occupation therapy, physiotherapy and clinical psychology care were provided to Ms Cheung.
Subjectively, she claimed that she felt better and had regularly taken an anti-depression medicine Fluoxetine.

treatments_future.treatment: Psychiatric follow up consultations at two monthly intervals for a period of one year (Hospital Authority charges $60 per consultation plus $10 medication every 16 weeks)
source: Dr Hung considered that consultation at two monthly intervals for a period of one year would be appropriate. The charges by the Hospital Authority were $60 per consultation plus $10 medication every 16 weeks.

treatments_future.treatment: Six sessions of follow up treatment at East Kowloon Psychiatric Centre (cost estimated at $600)
source: Dr Law on the other hand opined that Ms Cheung should continue to attend follow up treatments at the East Kowloon Psychiatric Centre for six sessions. The cost was estimated at $600.
